newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 4.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The Irish pound has hit its lowest level against sterling in almost six years following heavy selling by speculators scrambling to get out of many European currencies.

- John Bruton and Bertie Ahern, battling over who will be prime minister after Ireland's election on Friday, are conducting hours of rehearsals for a head-to-head television debate on Wednesday, believing there are still undecided voters to be won over.
- Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam told the opening session of multi-party talks that she wanted the issue of arms decommissioning resolved within weeks.
- The Lisheen mining development being developed by Minorco and Ivernia West has been granted planning permission.
- The Irish pound plunged to a six-year low against sterling as foreign exchange markets took fright at the prospect of a widely-based and weaker single European currency.
- Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats launched a final drive to secure the transfer votes they need to form the next government
- A man whose brain was damaged and who will need nursing for the rest of his life is to be paid 750,000 pounds and costs in settlement of a High Court action.
- Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern made a determined move to recover ground when he forced the Progressive Democrats to publicly abandon plans to cut 25,000 civil service jobs

- Independent radio stations were last night in the eye of a storm after they were warned they will lose their licences if they declare support for Fianna Fail on air in the runup to polling day on Friday.
- European police have launched an investigation aimed at breaking a Madrid-based racket which is flooding hundreds of Romanina gypsies into Ireland.
